subject: Food Science
title: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act
description: One-minute skill: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act.

hook.text: FSMA was the biggest overhaul of US food safety law in 70 years. It shifted focus from reacting to outbreaks to preventing them.

buildup.text: Signed in 2011, FSMA gives the FDA authority to require preventive controls, mandate recalls, and inspect foreign facilities.

discovery.text: Before FSMA, the FDA couldn't force a recall—only request one. Now mandatory recall authority means faster consumer protection.

twist.text: FSMA exempts small farms selling directly to consumers—farmers' market vendors follow different rules than supermarket suppliers.

climax.text: FSMA requires importers to verify foreign suppliers meet US standards. 15% of US food is imported—previously barely inspected.

punchline.text: Don't react to outbreaks—prevent them. FSMA rewrote the US food safety playbook.

quiz.question: What was the major shift in approach that FSMA introduced?
options: Focus shifted from reacting to outbreaks to preventing them
